recommended: and with it to provide three months’ pay for the army, and to add tens of thousands of measures of grain.
reason: δοῦσι…μισθοδοτῆσαι: the fifty talents are the three months’ pay. Bare μυριάδας rendered “tens of thousands”; a numeral may have dropped out, so the editor may add [...].

recommended: afterward to make his move toward Syria without any advance warning
reason: δίχα προόδου is obscure (literally “without advance/going forward”). Took it as suddenness, following ἄφνω καὶ παραδόξως; “circuitous route” has no basis in the Greek.

recommended: especially among the Etruscans and the Gauls
reason: The edition brackets [τὴν παλαίαν] as spurious, so it is omitted. “Along the coast” rests only on the conjecture παραλίαν and is not in the text.
Σκιπίωνα is singular; kept as transmitted. The apposition “naval victors” fits neither cleanly; probably corrupt (L. Scipio plus L. Aemilius Regillus?). Editor may add a note.

recommended: Calling this man king and blood of gods [...] making use of [...] that they would obtain some pity and pardon for [...] the king [...]
reason: Damaged papyrus: only surviving words kept, gaps marked. The conditional, “perhaps” and “what had happened” were invented. The rest of the paragraph after this span also smooths over gaps.

recommended: the remaining one to Tenedos, on which [...] Timagoras sailed as commander
reason: The text has a gap (*) before Τιμαγόρας. It may have held “another” or a different name, so the gap is marked and not resolved.

recommended: He also persuaded the Rhodians to join in the war.
reason: The subject is Perseus, not the embassy. The aorist is rendered as written. It conflicts with Rhodes’ later conduct (chs. 10–11), so a conative reading (“tried to persuade”) or corruption is possible.

recommended: [...] Polybius says [...] that [...] finer than this [...] and this has been said by the poet: [...] And turning at once and grasping my right hand, he said, “Polybius, it is a fine thing; but somehow I fear and foresee that someday someone else will give this same order about our own country.”
reason: Kept the legible fragments and Scipio’s speech, which had been omitted. The quotation the colon announces is missing (marked). The break after ταύτης δὲ falls in the next sentence, outside this span.
